answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to lock a stake in a shared escrow before it may trade, like a harbor that only lets ships dock after they post a bond. The stake acts as a slow glacier: creating thousands of fake identities becomes expensive because every identity must freeze real capital, and the cost grows with each new account. Honest agents that behave well can later bridge their locked stake into reputation credits, while attackers who burn their stake lose it permanently. This makes mass fake identities economically irrational.
